# King Iron Works

> King Iron Works designs, fabricates and installs custom ironwork: staircases (floating, spiral, curved), interior and exterior railings, fire escapes (installation, repair and inspection), gates, fences, balconies, structural steel and historic restoration. Headquarters and fabrication shop: 69 Norman St, Unit 20, Everett, MA 02149; serving Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Maine, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Vermont, New York and South Florida.

- Phone: +1 617-404-2589 · Text: +1 617-404-2589
- Free estimates: https://kingsironworks.com/contact
- Locations: https://kingsironworks.com/locations

## Guides
- [Massachusetts Fire Escape Inspection Requirements: The Complete 2026 Guide](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/massachusetts-fire-escape-inspection-requirements-2026): Massachusetts law mandates fire escape inspections every five years. Learn what's required, who can inspect, consequences of non-compliance, and how to prepare.
- [5 Warning Signs Your Fire Escape Needs Immediate Repair](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/warning-signs-fire-escape-needs-repair): Rust, loose railings, sagging platforms? Learn the 5 warning signs that mean your fire escape needs repair now — before it becomes a safety hazard or code violation.
- [Fire Escape Installation for Commercial Buildings: What Property Managers Need to Know](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/fire-escape-installation-commercial-buildings): Need a new fire escape for your apartment building or commercial property? Here's the complete guide to code requirements, the installation process, managing tenants, and what affects cost.
- [What Happens If Your Boston Building Fails a Fire Escape Inspection?](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/failed-fire-escape-inspection-boston): Failed your fire escape inspection in Massachusetts? Here's exactly what happens next — fines, legal exposure, insurance risk, mortgage complications, and how to get back into compliance fast.
- [Historic Ironwork Restoration in Beacon Hill: Preserving Boston's Architectural Heritage](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/historic-ironwork-restoration-beacon-hill): Beacon Hill's historic ironwork tells the story of Boston's earliest architecture. Learn how period-accurate restoration preserves your property's value and meets commission requirements.
- [South End Ironwork: A Guide to Boston's Largest Victorian Iron Collection](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/south-end-victorian-ironwork-guide): The South End has the largest collection of Victorian residential ironwork in the country. Learn about its history, unique characteristics, common issues, and how to restore it properly.
- [The Complete Guide to Custom Iron Railings for Boston Brownstones](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/custom-iron-railings-boston-brownstones): Planning new railings for your brownstone? From architectural style matching to building code requirements and historic commission approval, here's everything you need to know.
- [Wrought Iron vs. Steel: Which Is Right for Your Property?](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/wrought-iron-vs-steel): Choosing between wrought iron and steel for your railings, fences, or gates? Boston's ironwork experts break down durability, cost, aesthetics, and maintenance — especially for New England's climate.
- [Iron Security Gates for Boston Storefronts: Style Meets Safety](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/iron-security-gates-boston-storefronts): Protecting your storefront doesn't mean uglifying it. Learn about security gate types, historic district requirements, ADA compliance, and why custom iron gates are worth the investment.
- [How to Maintain Your Iron Railings Through New England Winters](https://kingsironworks.com/blog/maintain-iron-railings-new-england-winters): New England winters are brutal on ironwork. Here's the practical, season-by-season maintenance routine that keeps your railings protected from road salt, freeze-thaw cycles, and rust.
